Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Gameplay 2.1 Phase 2 3 Scoring Overview The game is divided into two phases. In the first phase, you will connect terminals and buildings with track tiles. In the second phase, you control your trolley from terminal to terminal and make the necessary stops in between. The first one to do so wins the game. Gameplay In phase 1, players take turns to place 2 tiles on the board, until you decide to move on to phase 2. When placing, each tile must be placed on to an empty space of the board or replace a tile with brown background. Green tiles cannot be replaced. When replacing a brown tile, it must make the same connections as the existing one. When planning your route, keep in mind that your streetcar will only go forward and can only do turns less than 90 degrees. Tracks can never : - Lead off the board; - Lead into a building; - Have end(s) that cannot be continued. To fulfill a route, connect one terminal that matches your number to the other terminal that matches your number on the other side of the board, passing by each of the three stops. You can pass the stops in any order Once the route is fulfilled, you may select to start phase 2. From now on, you will act with phase 2 rules. In a deviation from the published rules, in the BGA version, once a player places their train, their tiles become available for folks who are still placing tiles. Phase 2 Roll 3 dice and choose 1 to execute, then you can choose to pass or roll 2 dice and execute 1. Then you can choose to pass or roll 1 dice to execute. Then your turn ends. The dice have the following meaning: Red Light - Trolley does not move. One Green Lights - Trolley moves ahead one space. Two Green Lights (2 faces) - Trolley moves ahead two spaces. H - Trolley moves to next stop or terminal spot. Tools - Trolley must go back to last station or terminal for repairs. This also ends the player's turn. In a deviation from the published rules, in the BGA version, there are 2x Two Green Light faces and 1x Tools face. Scoring The current BGA version allows all players to play until the very end. As soon as a player reaches the destination station with their tram, they receive 1 point for each milestone that their opponents have not yet reached. The key milestones are: Placing the tram on the game board. Each of the stops indicated on their task card (2 or 3, depending on player count). Reaching the destination station. If someone presses the “Give Up” button, they lose the game with 0 points. Given a a secret set of stations and trolley line, players use tiles to build a common network of track.  They attempt to build a path that travels from one terminal to the other while passing the required stations.  After all their connections are made, a player may begin to race their trolley through the network. The first player to race their trolley from one terminal to the other and visit all their required stations wins.

The game was originally published as Linie 1 by Goldsieber.  In 1996, it was published by Mayfair as Streetcar with different end-game rules and artwork.  Later, it was published by Olsen in Sweden as San Francisco, again with different artwork.  Some versions, e.g. the Finnish one, seem to accommodate 2-6 players.
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Seemed pretty good at first, because it’s interactive! But then all the problems emerged. The track laying is just tedious logic-checking. Interaction is merely getting in others’ way, usually by accident. So it’s not even social interaction (just extending the playtime to double the length because players are NoT EfFiCiEnT, wheeee). And then you resolve the efficiency test with a…. dice-off? What? I fucking hated this game, it’s just a mess. Like today’s eurogames, just a shambling mess of random body parts that can barely stand on its own.

[Rating: 2/10] This one has never "clicked" with us.  We haul it out every couple of years just to remember why it sits on the shelf. (Mayfair version)

[Rating: 2/10] Building track seems to be difficult as anyone can tear up your work and cost you valuable time just to be mean.

[Rating: 3/10] Remade as Streetcar.  Players race to complete a tram line across town, then race that tram from start to finish.  Almost like two different games bolted together and it didn't quite work.

[Rating: 3/10] Couldn't quite decide if it was slightly better or slightly worst than Transamerica. There is no control whatsoever about the path your metro will take, and the game takes forever to complete. The movement of the cars at the end of the game is completely superflous and adds even more time to the game, even though absolutely no decisions can be taken during that phase.

[Rating: 3/10] Crazy boring.  The movement rules at the end were so so dumb.  I have no idea where the fun in this game was.  Well, It's gone now.  Shouldn't dwell on the past.

[Rating: 3/10] Dressed up abstract strategy with rules problems. Analysis paralysis factor is quite high.
